explanation: The mktime function converts a broken-down time structure (of type struct tm) into a time_t value representing the calendar time in seconds since the Epoch (January 1, 1970). It is used to normalize and convert local time components into a standard time format for calculations, comparisons, or storage in C programs.
code_example: timeStruct.tm_isdst = -1; // Daylight saving time not set
example_explanation: This example initializes a struct tm for January 1, 2023, calls mktime to convert it to a time_t value, and prints the result if successful, demonstrating how mktime transforms a broken-down time structure into a calendar time representation while handling potential errors.
